classification.difficultyReason: Establish continuity and compare derivatives of the constant and quadratic pieces at their join.

spec.description: Blue horizontal left ray meets the red quadratic right branch at the filled point (4,-1). Integer ticks and source axis ranges are retained.
spec.mathematics: y=-1 for x<4 and y=(x-4)^2-1 for x>=4.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible in the question edition.

answer.short: Yes. The branches join at $(4,-1)$ and both have gradient $0$ there.
answer.worked:
Let $g(x)=-1$ and $h(x)=x^2-8x+15$.
First test continuity:
$$\begin{aligned}g(4)&=-1\\h(4)&=4^2-8(4)+15\\h(4)&=-1\end{aligned}$$
The branches join at $x=4$, so $f$ is continuous there.
Differentiate and compare the branch gradients:
$$\begin{aligned}g'(x)&=0\\h'(x)&=2x-8\\g'(4)&=0\\h'(4)&=2(4)-8=0\end{aligned}$$
The gradients agree, so $f$ is differentiable at $x=4$.
